checklist_items.1.1: On first open the new-network dialog shows four textboxes, three checkboxes, and four button radios. There is no spinbutton, no combobox, and no unit. Name is an empty required textbox with maximum length 64 and no placeholder. Description is an empty textbox with maximum length 256, is not required, and has no placeholder. Roles is one required checkbox group. Its three localized role checkboxes are enabled and unchecked. Type is one radio group and is not required. Its four localized type labels are visible button radios, and host_ethernet is checked. With that default the default CIDR and the default interface are visible empty textboxes, are not required, and have no maximum length. The CIDR placeholder is 10.20.0.0/16. The interface placeholder is the localized glob example. Bootstrap CIDR and the advanced section are absent. The create POST sends the typed name, an empty description, role compute, type host_ethernet, an empty cidr, and an empty interface. The independent GET stores those same fields.
checklist_items.1.2: On first open the create dialog shows an empty name, host ethernet selected, and every role unchecked, and those fields are present immediately with no loading gate before Save. An empty name is rejected on the name field and sends no network create. The edit dialog has no password field. After the minimum create, the networks list row's edit control is one text button. Opening it backfills that name, an empty description, an empty CIDR, an empty interface, host ethernet, and the compute role, and the other roles stay unchecked. Cancel closes it and sends no further network write.
checklist_items.1.3: Name and roles are the required fields. Submitting an empty name and submitting a whitespace-only name each show the name-required error on the name field, mark that field invalid, and send no network create. With the name role-probe filled and no role selected, Save shows the role-required error, leaves the name valid, and sends no network create. The roles control is a checkbox group, so an empty string and whitespace are not role values.
checklist_items.1.7: The minimum create fills only the required name and the required compute role. Description, CIDR, and interface stay empty. Save sends POST /api/v1/networks with that name, an empty description, role compute, type host_ethernet, an empty cidr, and an empty interface, and the response is 201. The networks list row shows that name and the localized no-selector sentence. The detail page shows that name, an empty CIDR, an empty interface, and the localized not-attached sentence. The attach control on that page is one small button. After refresh the detail heading is still that name. The independent GET returns the same name, an empty description, role compute, type host_ethernet, an empty cidr, and an empty interface.
checklist_items.1.8: The minimum create leaves description, CIDR, and interface blank. That POST carries empty strings for those fields, and the independent GET stores them empty. A second create fills the description east lane, the CIDR 10.77.0.0/16, the interface ens*, and the roles storage_sync, compute, and serving. That save returns 201. The independent GET stores that description, that CIDR, that interface, type host_ethernet, and those roles. The detail page shows that description, that CIDR, and that interface. The selector on the minimum detail page is one small table.
checklist_items.1.9: While the create POST is held the save button stays loading and a second click sends no further create. The later 201 is the only stored network
checklist_items.1.10: The 502 keeps the create dialog and the name and roles, shows upstream fixture is unreachable, and stores no network. The retry 201 matches the independent detail GET
checklist_items.1.11: covered: Cancel, close and Escape each close the create dialog immediately, with no unsaved-changes prompt and no network write, so the stored networks stay unchanged
checklist_items.1.13: A role the Accelerator RDMA type cannot carry shows one tooltip with the localized reason. While the host Ethernet storage sync network's edit dialog is open on the empty description, another session's PUT sets that description to Other session and returns 200. The independent GET stores Other session. The dialog still shows the empty description, the same name, the same role, and the same type. There is no conflict status. Saving that dialog returns 200 with the empty description, and the independent GET returns the empty description with the same name, role, type, CIDR, and interface.
checklist_items.1.14: covered: After create, the independent detail GET matches the saved name, type, roles and empty address fields. Reload opens edit with that type and those roles. This definition attaches no agent or workload
checklist_items.1.15: Tab from the name field reaches the description. Enter in the empty name shows the name error and sends no network create. checklist_items.12.7: Delete confirmation carries both the name and the consequence, proven on this case's own scoped network rather than borrowed from the sibling network case: the confirmation string is the product's own, with {{name}} replaced, and it must be visible inside the viewport before the delete proceeds, so the copy asserted is 'Delete network <name>? Running instances keep the network they started with'. Reference blocking has no object on this resource, and the evidence is the surrounding error vocabulary rather than an absence of tests: writeNetworkErr (internal/server/api/networks.go:245) maps invalid, dedicated-unavailable, attachment-not-found, not-found, name-taken and attachment-exists and nothing in the in-use family, while errors.go defines SERVED_NAME_IN_USE, MODEL_IN_USE, IMAGE_IN_USE and STORAGE_IN_USE on four other resources and never NETWORK_IN_USE; Store.DeleteNetwork (internal/server/store/network_objects.go:98) removes the row together with its attachments and test runs in one transaction, so an attached network is deleted rather than refused. That is measured here: a node and two networks are created over the API, both attached, resolved_node_count reads 1, and DELETE answers 200 {'status': 'deleted'} rather than 409. The allowed-cleanup half is the cascade, asserted with the node still present, the network answering 404, and its name immediately reused - which is what proves no attachment row outlived the network. The failed-delete half deletes a non-existent id, requires 404 NETWORK_NOT_FOUND, and re-reads the second network afterwards with its attachment count and its name, description, CIDR, interface, roles and type required to be unchanged; 404 alone would show that an error was reported, not that nothing else moved. The copy states the consequence for running instances and does not mention the released attachment, recorded as an observation about the copy rather than asserted as a defect.
